alignments.note: The ASV recasts the noun עָבְי as the predicate adjective "thick".

Recasting "its thickness was a handbreadth" as "it was a handbreadth thick" leaves the suffix realized by the subject pronoun (rule 40); reading "it" as a dummy subject on the copula, with the suffix unrepresented, stays defensible.
Verbless clause: the supplied copula joins the predicate that licenses it (rule 20), and the indefinite "a" belongs to the noun (rule 15).
The "the" of "the brim thereof" is supplied by the possessive construction and rests on the noun.
מַעֲשֵׂה is rendered verbally as "wrought"; the supplied copula joins that predicate (rule 20).
Construct noun takes only its own English word plus the supplied article (rule 29).
The "of" of the construct chain belongs to the nomen rectum (rule 19).
פֶּרַח שׁוֹשָׁן is asyndetic; the second "like" is the function word the ASV supplies for the comparative accusative and rests on the noun (rule 33) rather than being added.
The dual אַלְפַּיִם is one token rendered "two thousand", headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun and verb (rule 17).
